messages.subject: error when using  inla.zmarginal
parts:
> I met an error when using inla.zmarginal function. It shows :

> Error in seq.default(2, n - 1, by = 2) : wrong sign in 'by' argument

> 

> The code I used is as follows.

> n=65536 #256*256

> formula= x ~ 1+ f(node, model="matern2d", nu=1, nrow=dim(y)[1], ncol=dim(y)[1])+f(node2,model='iid')

> ##20 minuter for 128*128

> result=inla(formula, family='binomial', Ntrials=1,data=list(x=x,node=node,node2=node2),

>              control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE)

>              #,control.inla = list(tolerance = 1e-10, h = 1e-04)

>              )

> 

> y.mean=rep(NA,n)

> for(i in (1:n)){

>    temp=inla.zmarginal(result$marginals.fitted.values[[i]],silent = TRUE)

>    y.mean[i]=temp[[1]]

> }

> 

> Do you know how to fix this problem?

> 

> This code is ok when I tried a smaller image data where n=128*128

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] error when using  inla.zmarginal
parts:
Hi

you must add 'control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE)' to also compute
the fitted values (and the linear predictor)

Best,
H

PS: The SPDE models somewhat better suited for such models, see the
SPDE tutorials at r-inla.org

if there is an error in 'seq(2,n-1,by=2)' and 'wrong sign', that means
that n <= 2.

> n=2; seq(2,n-1,by=2)

got it. its a singular point (numerically). probably coming from
some kind of ''defect'' in the model. so its bascially just a
singleton, which makes everything crash.

you can compute what you want from the posterior for the linear
predictor instead (at location 2441), but likely this is causes by
something weird in the model and/or datainput
